newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: S&P cuts Bank Ayudhya short-term rating.
newsitem.headline: S&P cuts Bank Ayudhya short-term rating.

text.p: Standard & Poor's said on Wednesday it affirmed its "BBB" long-term counterparty rating on Thailand's Bank of Ayudhya Plc and has lowered the short-term counterparty rating to "A3" from "A2".
S&P said the ratings had been removed from CreditWatch, where they were placed on March 18.
The rating outlook was negative, reflecting concerns that the economic downturn and resulting asset quality problems would be higher and more prolonged than anticipated, it said.
S&P said it had some concerns about the deteriorating condition of Thailand's financial sector following the downturn in the property market and a slowdown in the economy.
The affirmation of Bank of Ayudhya's long-term rating recognised its position as one of the larger and better performing Thai commercial banks.
S&P said Bank of Ayudhya's long-term rating already reflected its slightly higher vulnerability to industry downturns compared with its higher rated peers.

"Despite Bank of Ayudhya's current satisfactory liquidity position, the downgrade of the bank's short-term rating recognises system-wide liquidity concerns in Thailand and the bank's higher vulnerability to these relative to its peers," it said.
